prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realisation of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms confined at the magic wavelength allow frequency measurements at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from B038 to B046, and I want to be plain about why. My test is whether I can be absolutely sure that the topic is right and that the people credited did the original work. For B046 I can: Katori proposed magic-wavelength trapping and his group made the first strontium lattice clock, and the Ye group then carried it to the 1e-18 regime and to many-body clock physics. The result is reproduced and compared at JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and elsewhere, by people who did not build the original apparatus. It is exactly the kind of tool that opens a door, since millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, tests of constants and dark-matter searches were not accessible before, and the Statutes name invention as well as discovery. The two-name credit needs no defence against its own omissions beyond a short, honest note about Lemonde and Takamoto, which a narrowly worded citation can carry. B038 remains a scientifically excellent candidate and I would not oppose it, but its credit problem cannot be fixed inside a three-name limit.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection to B046 is still novelty against the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 prize on single quantum systems. I now think the answer is the one Lindroth and Johansson gave: the comb is a ruler and the 2012 work is control of single ions, whereas the lattice clock is a different physical idea, many neutral atoms interrogated at once with Doppler and recoil effects suppressed, and the citation must say so explicitly. Second, priority within the field is not fully settled from what we have: Lemonde (SYRTE), Takamoto and Ludlow all contributed and the priority history is recalled from memory, not checked against the 2001 to 2006 papers. Third, it is an instrument and its fundamental-physics output so far consists of limits and demonstrations, not findings; I accept that as a real distinction from B038, which I weighted heavily in round 1, but the Statutes do not make it disqualifying.

responses.point: Kroll corrected my statement that Ye shares the 2005 prize, recalling that the laureates were Glauber, Hall and Hansch and that Ye, as Hall's postdoc, was not a laureate. He also rejected waiting for the SI redefinition of the second.
responses.response: You are right on the record and I withdraw the premise. The 2005 prize went to Glauber, Hall and Hansch; Ye was in Hall's group and was not a laureate, so there is no second prize to the same person and that part of the overlap argument disappears. On the redefinition I also move to your side. I raised waiting as a reason to put B046 behind B038, but the instrument's performance is verified in many laboratories and the science does not depend on a metrology-body timetable, so I no longer count it against acting now. I hold one reservation. Because you disclose a close link to the Ye group, I would ask that the discussion of Lemonde, Takamoto and Ludlow be led by members without that link, and I would be comfortable with you declaring and voting.

responses.point: Lindroth argued that the lattice clock is a different physical idea from the 2005 comb and the 2012 single-ion work, and that the citation should name the magic-wavelength lattice concept explicitly. She also asked whether the Statutes' test is applied evenly to B038 and B046.
responses.response: This is the answer to my own round-1 worry. I asked that B046 be judged on the same test as B038, and on that test it holds: original proposal, original first realisation, independent reproduction. I agree the citation must name the lattice and the magic wavelength, not just precision, so it cannot be read as a third reward for the comb. On your question of Ye alone versus a third name, I would not add Lemonde or Takamoto. The three-name limit would force a choice among several real contributors, and Katori with Ye cover the concept, the first demonstration group and the accuracy record. I would record in the minutes why the others are not named, as you suggest.

responses.point: Eriksson agreed to keep a B038 citation narrow to the 2D quantum spin Hall state and to state the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang gap openly. He ranks B038 above B046 on conceptual novelty, not merit.
responses.response: I agreed with that narrow wording in round 1 and I still think it is the best B038 could do. My difficulty is that a narrow citation does not close the gap. Molenkamp's experiment was designed around the BHZ proposal, which is an original contribution that a three-name limit leaves out, and the 3D work sits beside it. I cannot tell the world that we are absolutely sure we identified the original contributors in that case. I accept your point that Z2 time-reversal-invariant topology differs from the 2016 prize, which was about invariants with broken time reversal and about defects, so I no longer treat overlap as a decisive objection. Attribution is what moves me, not novelty.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, noted that B046 was the only candidate five of eight members placed in their top three, and wanted the citation worded around the lattice invention and a narrow credit.
responses.response: I do not rely on support counts to settle the question, and I would reach the same view if the count were reversed. What persuades me is that the record of who did what first is cleanest here. I support your wording. I would add that the minutes should say which parts of the clock story are not being credited, so that the citation does not imply Katori and Ye built every clock.

uncertainties: Priority history among Katori, Takamoto, Lemonde and Ye is recalled from memory and has not been checked against the primary papers; I would want that checked before a final vote.

Whether the committee will accept the one-sentence novelty answer relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and whether I am giving too little weight to the instrument-versus-discovery distinction I used in round 1.

If the committee prefers B038 after all, whether a citation limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall state can be defended without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang; I could support it only with that gap stated openly.
Whether B042 will become clearer once the superconducting mechanism is settled; I treat it as a later candidate.
statement.conflict_note: I have no personal link to Katori, Ye or the other B046 contributors. I note my earlier institutional proximity to Johansson at Chalmers, relevant only if B006 is revisited, in which case I would defer. I have no conflict on B038 or B042. I note Kroll's disclosed link to the Ye group and ask that it be handled in the open.
